name: NeuroSurge
source_lineage: Based on the 10 November 2026 camera-update preview. Adds display recovery in place of the stop on a refused frame, press-and-drag turning of the brain and mirror body, muscle clicks routed through the existing motor map, paper-ribbon orbit arrows at fixed places, a higher default brain placement, tissue-shaded motor areas, position-welded surface normals, a coordinated forearm and hip turn, a keyboard picture, removal of the floating own-face display, and faster crosshair picking and frame logic. Existing mesh files, asset notices, public provenance redactions and desktop launchers are retained.
anatomy_assets: 490 OBJ meshes retained from the preceding preview. BodyParts3D is CC BY 4.0; Z-Anatomy facial derivatives are CC BY-SA 4.0.
public_preview_authorized: 10 November 2026 user instruction: experimental previews for all projects
browser_verification: Author development checks only: scripted mouse and key input in one desktop Chromium on one pinned processor core, with screenshots, frame-interval counts and the DevTools sampling profiler, compared against the preceding preview under the same script. No independent review yet. Not checked: Firefox, Safari, touch, phones, screen readers, reduced-motion settings. This does not establish complete control, timing, joint-mechanics or physiological validation.
known_engineering_gaps: Independent browser review of this build has not been done
Looking around is the slowest path (about 35 frames a second in the author's single-core test, single frames up to about 0.1 s)
The look stops where the whole arm can no longer be shown; one rare case pauses for about a third of a second and turns the view part of the way back
Key-driven reach is unchanged: already at arm length, whole-hand-in-view and view-edge limits; a wider sweep needs a different hand-anchor design
A clicked muscle switches on a whole motor area and its movement's muscles, not one muscle; some muscles have no movement and only light an area
The leg turn rotates only the hips by 10 degrees; the right upper arm does not turn; hip rotator muscles are not coloured
The left shoulder girdle slides with the arm on both bodies; a slide, not a solved shoulder-blade rotation, and not compared with reference images
The brain's top arrow is partly off screen at the start view on wide screens; the left arrow can sit behind the arm
The retired floating-face code paths remain in the renderer, switched off
SHA256SUMS and release-manifest.json predate these source changes and must be regenerated before release
publication_status: Prepared for review. Not yet published; the release aggregates are stale until regenerated.
